verses.text: All the kings west of the Jordan heard about these things: the kings in the hill country, in the western foothills, and all along the coast of the Great Sea as far as Lebanon. They were the kings of the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites.
They joined together as one to fight against Joshua and Israel.
But when the people of Gibeon heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and Ai,
they came up with a trick. They pretended to be messengers from far away. They loaded their donkeys with worn-out sacks and old wineskins that were cracked and mended.
They wore old patched sandals and old clothes. All the bread they carried was dry and mouldy.
They went to Joshua in the camp at Gilgal and said to him and the men of Israel, "We have come from a country far away. Please make a peace treaty with us."
The men of Israel said to these Hivites, "But maybe you live near us. How can we make a treaty with you?"
They said to Joshua, "We are your servants." Joshua asked, "Who are you, and where do you come from?"
They answered, "We, your servants, have come from a very distant country because of the fame of the LORD your God. We have heard all about him and everything he did in Egypt,
and what he did to the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan: Sihon king of Heshbon, and Og king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth.
So our leaders and all the people of our country told us, 'Take food for the journey. Go and meet them and say, We are your servants. Please make a treaty with us.'
This bread was still warm when we packed it at home on the day we left to come to you. But look how dry and mouldy it is now.
These wineskins were new when we filled them, but look how cracked they are. Our clothes and sandals are worn out from the very long journey."
The Israelites tasted some of their food, but they did not ask the LORD what to do.
So Joshua made peace with them and a treaty to let them live, and the leaders of the people swore an oath to keep it.
Three days after making the treaty, the Israelites heard that these people were their neighbours, living close by.
So the Israelites set out, and on the third day they came to their towns: Gibeon, Kephirah, Beeroth and Kiriath Jearim.
But the Israelites did not attack them, because their leaders had sworn an oath to them by the LORD, the God of Israel. All the people grumbled against the leaders.
But the leaders answered, "We have sworn an oath to them by the LORD, the God of Israel, so we cannot touch them now.
This is what we will do: we will let them live, so that God's anger does not fall on us for breaking our oath."
The leaders said, "Let them live." So they became woodcutters and water carriers for all the people, as the leaders had decided.
Then Joshua called the Gibeonites and said, "Why did you trick us by saying, 'We live far away from you,' when you actually live right here among us?
Now you are under a curse. Some of you will always be servants, cutting wood and carrying water for the house of my God."

They answered Joshua, "We were told clearly that the LORD your God commanded his servant Moses to give you this whole land and to destroy all its people as you came. We were very afraid for our lives because of you, so we did this.
Now we are in your hands. Do to us whatever seems good and right to you."
So Joshua did that. He saved them from the Israelites, and they did not kill them.
That day Joshua made the Gibeonites woodcutters and water carriers for the people and for the altar of the LORD, at the place the LORD would choose. They still do this today.
